description: About, story, owner and team sections: who will actually show up at the house. Puts a named owner and real crew in front, tells a short, specific origin story and states what the business stands for.
queries: team section for a small business
founder letter section with portrait and signature

references.layout: A narrow centred column (~260px measure) under a two-line centred headline, 'a letter from / our [photo] CEO', with a small pill-shaped portrait (~48×28) sitting inline between the words. Body paragraphs ~10px; halfway down, a large pull-quote (~20px) breaks out to a wider measure; it ends with a handwritten signature, a tiny flag and 'Proudly Canadian'.
references.type: Headline geometric sans ~34px regular, all lowercase; body sans ~10px at ~1.5 leading; pull-quote ~20px regular, centred.
references.color: Off-white ~#FBFBFB; text ~#111111; the small flag red ~#D52B1E is the only colour.
details: A pill portrait set inline in the headline, so the face and the words read as one
The lowercase headline gives a personal, unpretentious voice
The pull-quote widens past the body measure mid-letter
Script signature followed by a local-pride line with a tiny flag
references.why_it_works: The letter format makes the owner accountable and human, and the inline portrait is a crafted, memorable move that costs nothing to build.
references.trade_adaptation: 'a letter from / our [Mike's face] owner' for a family plumbing company, signed, ending 'Proudly serving Dayton since 1994'.

references.layout: A full-bleed photo (~16px radius) of the founder leaning, arms crossed, against a branded vehicle. A short quote (~12px serif) with name and title sits top-right in the soft sky area of the photo.
references.type: Quote serif ~13px white; name ~8px bold; title ~8px regular.
references.color: Natural daylight photo with a warm grade; text ~#FFFFFF over the soft, blurred sky.
details: The owner is photographed with the company vehicle and its logo, so the brand is in the scene instead of in a badge
The quote sits in empty space in the photo, with no overlay box
Shallow depth of field keeps the background soft enough for the text
references.why_it_works: It is the most adaptable image a trade has: owner, truck, logo, daylight. Placing the text in the photo's empty space feels editorial.
references.trade_adaptation: Owner leaning on the wrapped service van in a driveway; quote 'I still answer the phone myself.', Mike Torres, Owner. Hero of the About page.

references.layout: Centred headline and subline, then two columns. Left: three stats in handwriting-style numerals with sketchy circles and underlines and small grey pill labels, followed by four short paragraphs. Right: a polaroid-style photo (~8px white border, ~3° rotation, soft shadow) of the two founders, with a handwritten 'Emanuel & Pieter' and a hand-drawn arrow pointing at them.
references.type: Headline sans ~26px semibold; body ~11px; numerals and annotation in a marker/handwriting face ~36px; pill labels ~7px caps.
references.color: Light grey page ~#F6F6F6; handwriting and doodles amber ~#E8A33D; text ~#2A2A2A; pills ~#E4E4E4.
details: A hand-drawn annotation names the people in the photo
A slightly rotated print with a white border and a shadow
One surprising stat ('0 offices') adds personality
Doodled circles and sparks around the numbers
references.why_it_works: The annotations and tilted print make the founders feel like real people in a scrapbook, while the layout stays orderly.
references.trade_adaptation: A polaroid of 'Dave & his son Luke' with a marker arrow; stats '36 years', '2 generations', '0 subcontractors'. Great for friendly and rustic styles.

references.layout: Asymmetric. The serif title 'A note from the founders' sits top-left (~20px), the letter runs in a right-hand column (~45% width), and below it a small rotated photo of the founders on a sofa sits beside several handwritten signatures scattered loosely.
references.type: Title serif ~20px regular; body sans ~11px at ~1.55 leading.
references.color: White ground; text ~#1D1D1D; the photo supplies the colour (red sofa, navy wall).
details: Several signatures scattered and slightly overlapping: everyone signed
The photo is tilted a couple of degrees with a thin white border
The letter's origin story names a concrete place ('rented a room in an old fire station')
references.why_it_works: A short letter, a specific origin detail and real signatures make a credible About section that is easy to fill.
references.trade_adaptation: 'A note from the Hendersons' signed by both spouses; origin line: 'started with one van and a ladder in 1998'.

references.layout: The left half holds a huge two-line serif headline, 'Who / we are', with the second line indented; the right half holds two short paragraphs (~11px). Below, candid team photos are scattered at different sizes and offsets, bleeding off the bottom.
references.type: High-contrast display serif ~80px regular at ~0.95 leading; body sans ~11px.
references.color: Butter cream ~#FEF8E8; headline and body deep maroon ~#3A0E0E.
details: The indented second line gives the headline a staggered, editorial shape
The headline takes half the width while the copy is a narrow column, a big contrast in scale
Candid, mid-conversation photos rather than posed headshots
The copy mentions life outside work ('parents of humans, pets, and plants')
references.why_it_works: Pure typographic confidence. It makes a tiny company feel established without inventing stats.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Who / we are' or 'Since / 1972' for a family painter or landscaper, with candid crew photos scattered below.

references.layout: A 50/50 split. Left: a warm off-white panel with a tiny eyebrow, a large wide-set headline over two lines (~30px), a short paragraph and a single button at the bottom. Right: a full-bleed photo of the family (two parents and two kids) in front of a brick wall.
references.type: Wide/extended grotesk headline ~30px regular; body ~11px; eyebrow ~9px.
details: The headline 'Two businesses, one family, all together' makes the family the story
The photo bleeds to the section edge with no radius and no frame
The button is pinned to the bottom of the text panel, lining up with the photo's bottom edge
references.why_it_works: The plainest family-business layout that works: a real family photo, one strong line, one action.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Three generations, one phone number.' with a family photo on the shop steps; button 'Meet the crew'.

references.layout: Left-aligned serif 'Meet the team', then a horizontal row of tall cards (~200×300, ~6px radius). Each is a full-bleed portrait of someone seated and relaxed in a real space, with name and role bottom-left over a subtle gradient. One card in the row is a quote instead of a person.
references.type: Title serif ~20px; name and role serif ~11px in white.
references.color: White page; warm-toned photos; bottom gradient ~rgba(0,0,0,0.35).
details: People sit in real spaces, laughing or mid-thought, instead of standing against white backgrounds
Name and role in a small serif at bottom-left
A quote card placed among the portraits breaks the rhythm
references.why_it_works: It shows how to make team photos feel warm and premium, and the format scales from 3 to 20 people.
references.trade_adaptation: Crew members on the tailgate, in the shop, on a job site; cards read 'Carlos · Lead installer, 12 yrs'. Slot one customer quote card into the row.

references.layout: A small label and a witty subline top-left, then an 8-column grid of portraits with identical crops (~95×105), each with name and role/city on two small lines beneath. The first row is right-aligned, leaving whitespace at top-left.
references.type: Sans ~8px; name bold, role regular grey.
references.color: White ground; the photos are vintage childhood snapshots in faded film colour and black-and-white.
details: Every team member appears as a vintage childhood or young-adult photo, one concept that ties mismatched photos together
The subline 'Everybody, and their mother.' is a play on the company name
A uniform crop ratio keeps the grid tidy despite the varied sources
references.why_it_works: A single photo concept turns a generic grid into a story, and it is easy to copy with old family photos.
references.trade_adaptation: Multi-generation business: show 'then' photos (Grandpa's first truck, 1974) alongside today's crew, all with the same crop, under an 'Est. 1974' subline.

references.layout: Two columns divided by a single vertical rule. Left: a large statement (~22px) whose last word is grey. Right: a vertical roster where each row has a square headshot (~86px, ~6px radius, grey backdrop), the name with tiny blue language-pill tags, the role in grey, and a one-line description aligned to the bottom of the photo.
references.type: Grotesk; statement ~22px medium; names ~11px semibold; role ~11px grey; description ~7px.
references.color: Light grey ~#EBEBEB; text ~#111111; secondary ~#8A8A8A; pills ~#1D4ED8 with white text.
details: Tiny pill tags beside each name show the languages spoken
The statement's last word is grey ('familial bond'), giving a two-tone headline
Each description sits on the photo's bottom line, so every row reads as one unit
references.why_it_works: A roster that scales, with small tags that are genuinely useful to customers.
references.trade_adaptation: Pills like 'ES' (speaks Spanish), 'Master Electrician', 'EPA 608'; a one-liner such as 'Handles all our heat-pump installs.'

references.layout: Two columns. Left: a tiny caps eyebrow, a bold heading (~22px), a cluster of images (a black booklet cover reading 'HUMAN FIRST' plus two photos) and a 'DOWNLOAD … (PDF)' pill button. Right: numbered rows divided by hairlines, each with a bold value (~15px), a one-line explanation and a small right-aligned index '/ 01'.
references.type: Heading grotesk bold ~22px; values ~15px bold; body ~10px; indices ~8px.
references.color: White ground; text ~#111111; hairlines ~#E2E2E2; booklet black with white condensed type.
details: The values are packaged as a named, downloadable document ('The Mews Constitution')
Slash-number indices ('/ 01') aligned right
Values written as two-part phrases ('Listen deeply, act boldly')
references.why_it_works: It treats values as a real document the business stands behind, and the list format is calm and easy to scan.
references.trade_adaptation: 'The Henderson Promise' as a downloadable PDF: '/01 Show up when we say', '/02 Protect your home (boot covers, drop cloths)', '/03 Price in writing before we start'.

references.layout: A full-bleed black section with ~10 white handwritten signatures scattered loosely across the upper two-thirds at varied sizes, and a two-line centred serif sentence beneath.
details: The whole team's signatures stand in for photos or logos
The line reads: 'We believe in creating work that we're proud to sign our name on.'
Signatures vary in scale and angle, giving an organic composition
references.why_it_works: It states pride in the work literally, which fits trades perfectly, where a craftsman signs off a job.
references.trade_adaptation: Every crew member's signature above 'Every job gets signed off by the person who did it.' Strong for industrial and premium styles.

references.layout: A centred paragraph (~14px) at the top; below it, a landscape candid photo of the two founders clinking bottles, framed with a thick black outline and ~16px radius and slightly rotated. Bubbly hand-lettered 'cheers!' overlaps the photo's bottom edge, and a monospace sign-off is centred beneath.
references.type: Paragraph grotesk ~14px medium; custom bubbly outlined lettering ~50px; sign-off monospace ~8px.
references.color: Saturated yellow ~#FFE53D ground; black ~#111111 outlines and text; lettering filled yellow with a black outline.
details: A hand-lettered word breaks out of the photo frame
The sign-off 'Smooches, Erin & George / Co-Founders & Partners' in monospace is warm and specific
A thick black outline makes the photo look like a sticker
references.why_it_works: A joyful, personal sign-off, showing how one custom word can carry a brand's personality.
references.trade_adaptation: For a friendly cleaning or pest-control brand: owner photo with hand-lettered 'thanks!', signed 'See you soon, Rosa & the crew'.

takeaways: Put a named owner in front: a real face, a real name, a real signature. Letters and sign-offs ('Stay dry, Mike') beat corporate mission statements.
Use environmental portraits (with the truck, in the shop, on the job), not white-background headshots.
Specific origin details (a place, a year, the first vehicle) make the story believable.
A big typographic statement next to a narrow body column is the cheapest way to look premium.
Add one crafted, hand-made touch per section: a signature, a handwritten annotation or a tilted print.
For teams, use a uniform crop and one unifying concept, and add useful tags (languages, licenses, years on the job) instead of LinkedIn icons.
Present values as a short numbered list or a named promise document the business stands behind.
avoid: Grids of identical circular headshots with LinkedIn icons (Origin, Slash, Coda)
Generic value cards with emoji or icon circles ('Customer First', 'Integrity', 'Excellence') (Workable, HoneyBook)
A big group photo inside a carousel with dots (Customer.io)
Team cards styled as browser windows or UI mockups (Daydream): SaaS cosplay
Stock imagery of a diverse team high-fiving in an office
Huge vanity stats (team size, countries) where a small trade would be better served by years, jobs and generations
